item.title: How, Ānanda, is it that four foundations of mindfulness, when developed and cultivated, perfect the seven factors of enlightenment? Whenever, Ānanda, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating…
item.description:
How, Ānanda, is it that four foundations of mindfulness, when developed and cultivated, perfect the seven factors of enlightenment? Whenever, Ānanda, a bhikkhu dwells contemplating the body as a body, his mindfulness is established; at that time, Ānanda, a bhikkhu is mindful, not forgetful. Whenever, Ānanda, a bhikkhu abides mindful, not forgetful, then the mindfulness enlightenment factor is aroused in that bhikkhu. Whenever, Ānanda, a bhikkhu develops the mindfulness enlightenment factor, then, through development, the mindfulness enlightenment factor comes to fulfillment. Abiding thus mindful, he wisely investigates, examines, and contemplates that Dhamma.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 54.13

item.title: Bhikkhus, I say that almsfood is of two kinds: to be used and not to be used — thus it has been said. For what…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, I say that almsfood is of two kinds: to be used and not to be used — thus it has been said. For what reason is it said? Here, if one knows of a certain almsfood: 'This almsfood, when I use it, unwholesome states increase and wholesome states decrease' — then such almsfood should not be used. Here, if one knows of a certain almsfood: 'This almsfood, when I use it, unwholesome states decrease and wholesome states increase' — then such almsfood should be used.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 10.54

item.title: The Blessed One: Having seen craving, discontent, and greed, There can be no desire for sexual intercourse. Why would I desire this thing Full of…
item.description:
The Blessed One:
Having seen craving, discontent, and greed,
There can be no desire for sexual intercourse.
Why would I desire this thing
Full of urine and excrement, which I would touch with my foot?

From: Sutta Nipāta 4.9

item.title: Bhikkhus, the Dhamma has been well taught by me, made manifest, opened up, shown, and stripped of its old wrappings. Because the Dhamma has been…
item.description:
Bhikkhus, the Dhamma has been well taught by me, made manifest, opened up, shown, and stripped of its old wrappings. Because the Dhamma has been well taught by me, made manifest, opened up, shown, and stripped of its old wrappings, for those bhikkhus who are Arahants, with taints destroyed, who have lived the holy life, done what had to be done, laid down the burden, reached the goal, destroyed the fetters of existence, liberated by final knowledge — the cycle of rebirth cannot be traced for them.

From: Majjhima Nikāya 22 – Alagaddūpamasutta

item.title: Elder Nun Anopamā: Born in a high family, With many jewels and riches, Complete with beautiful complexion, Majjha's beloved daughter. Courted by a king's son,…
item.description:
Elder Nun Anopamā:

Born in a high family,
With many jewels and riches,
Complete with beautiful complexion,
Majjha's beloved daughter.

Courted by a king's son,
Asked in marriage by a rich man's son,
Messengers came to my father:
'Give me Anopamā.'

The princess, your daughter,
Weigh her — how much is she worth?
I will give eight times
That amount in pure gold and jewels.

I saw the Awakened One,
The Blessed One, unsurpassed,
I bowed at his feet,
Approached and sat to one side.

Out of compassion, Gotama
Taught me the Dhamma.
Right there on that seat,
I attained the third fruit.

Then I shaved my hair,
Went forth into homelessness.
Today, on the seventh night,
Craving has been washed away.

From: Therīgāthā 6.5

item.title: One who develops loving-kindness, Mindful, immeasurable, The fetters grow thin, He sees the destruction of attachments. With a mind not cruel, Compassionate toward all beings,…
item.description:
One who develops loving-kindness,
Mindful, immeasurable,
The fetters grow thin,
He sees the destruction of attachments.
With a mind not cruel,
Compassionate toward all beings,
Therefore he becomes
A perfectly pure, excellent one.
With a mind of compassion
Toward all beings,
The noble one well performs
Much good merit.
Having conquered
A great multitude of people,
Kings and sages
By sacrificial rites,
The horse sacrifice, human sacrifice,
The victory-drinking sacrifice,
The luck-throwing sacrifice,
The locked-door sacrifice.
They do not reach one-sixteenth
Of one well developed in loving-kindness,
As the light of the moon
Outshines all the stars.
He does not kill, nor cause to kill,
Does not conquer, nor cause to conquer,
With loving-kindness toward all beings,
He has enmity toward none.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 8.1

item.title: With birth as condition, bhikkhus, aging and death come to be. With existence as condition, bhikkhus, birth comes to be. With clinging as condition, bhikkhus,…
item.description:
With birth as condition, bhikkhus, aging and death come to be. With existence as condition, bhikkhus, birth comes to be. With clinging as condition, bhikkhus, existence comes to be. With craving as condition, bhikkhus, clinging comes to be. With feeling as condition, bhikkhus, craving comes to be. With contact as condition, bhikkhus, feeling comes to be. With the six sense bases as condition, bhikkhus, contact comes to be. With name-and-form as condition, bhikkhus, the six sense bases come to be. With consciousness as condition, bhikkhus, name-and-form comes to be. With formations as condition, bhikkhus, consciousness comes to be. With ignorance as condition, bhikkhus, formations come to be. Whether Tathāgatas arise or do not arise, that element still persists, that stableness of Dhamma, that fixed course of Dhamma, that specific conditionality. The Tathāgata fully awakens to this, fully realizes it. Having fully awakened to it, having fully realized it, he declares, teaches, proclaims, establishes, reveals, analyzes, clarifies, and illuminates it.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 12.20

item.title: Furthermore, bhikkhus, in the future there will be bhikkhus who are undeveloped in body, undeveloped in virtue, undeveloped in mind, undeveloped in wisdom. Because they…
item.description:
Furthermore, bhikkhus, in the future there will be bhikkhus who are undeveloped in body, undeveloped in virtue, undeveloped in mind, undeveloped in wisdom. Because they are undeveloped in body, undeveloped in virtue, undeveloped in mind, undeveloped in wisdom, the elder bhikkhus will live in abundance, lazy, leaders in decline, discarding the burden of seclusion, not making an effort to attain what has not been attained, to achieve what has not been achieved, to realize what has not been realized. And later generations will follow their wrong view. They will become those who live in abundance, lazy, leaders in decline, discarding the burden of seclusion, and will not make an effort to attain what has not been attained, to achieve what has not been achieved, to realize what has not been realized. Thus, bhikkhus, from defilement of the Dhamma comes defilement of the Discipline; from defilement of the Discipline comes defilement of the Dhamma. This, bhikkhus, is the fifth fear regarding the future, not yet arisen now but will arise in the future. You should fully understand them. Having fully understood them, you should strive to abandon that fear.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.79

item.title: Like the moon unstained Moving through the firmament, With radiance blazing Among the starry host in the world. So too, one of virtue, A person…
item.description:
Like the moon unstained
Moving through the firmament,
With radiance blazing
Among the starry host in the world.
So too, one of virtue,
A person with faith,
With giving, blazes forth
Among the stingy in the world.
Like a cloud with rain and thunder,
A garland with a hundred crests,
Filling up the valleys,
Spreading over the plains.
So too, full of vision,
A disciple of the Perfectly Enlightened One,
The wise one surpasses stinginess
In five respects:
Life span and fame,
Beauty and happiness,
With abundant wealth,
Upon death he enjoys heavenly bliss.

From: Aṅguttara Nikāya 5.31

item.title: - What illuminates the world? What awakens the world? Who works together with humans? What is their conduct? Who nourishes both the lazy and the…
item.description:
- What illuminates the world?
What awakens the world?
Who works together with humans?
What is their conduct?
Who nourishes both the lazy and the diligent,
Like a mother her child?
What beings sustain their lives
Depending on the earth?
- Wisdom illuminates the world,
Right mindfulness awakens the world,
Cattle work together with humans,
The plough is their path.
Rain nourishes both the lazy and the diligent,
Like a mother her child.
Rain sustains beings' lives,
Depending on the earth.

From: Saṃyutta Nikāya 1.80
